ai.literal: Army, subjects, wealth, ministry, allies, fortress—all these six, he who possesses, among kings, is a bull.
ai.translation: He who possesses these six elements—an army, subjects, wealth, ministers, allies, and fortresses—is a bull among kings.
ai.modern: படை, குடிமக்கள், செல்வம், அமைச்சர், நட்பு நாடுகள், அரண் ஆகிய ஆறு அங்கங்களையும் உடையவன் அரசர்களுள் ஆண் சிங்கம் போன்றவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the six essential components of a well-governed state. A ruler must have a strong army, loyal subjects, abundant resources, wise ministers, reliable allies, and secure fortifications. The word 'kūḻ' literally refers to food or grain, but in this context of statecraft, it represents the treasury and resources of the land. The poet uses the metaphor of 'ēṟu' (a strong bull or male beast) to describe a ruler who possesses all six elements as a majestic leader among peers.

ai.literal: Fearlessness, generosity, wisdom, energy—these four, without failing, to rulers, are natural characteristics.
ai.translation: Fearlessness, generosity, wisdom, and tireless energy—these four qualities, without ever failing, are the natural attributes of a ruler.
ai.modern: அச்சமின்மை, கொடைத்தன்மை, அறிவு, ஊக்கம் ஆகிய இந்த நான்கும் குறையாமல் இருப்பதுவே அரசர்களுக்குரிய இயல்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet lists the four fundamental qualities that a ruler must possess. 'அஞ்சாமை' represents the courage to face challenges, while 'ஈகை' is the generosity to support subjects. 'அறிவு' denotes the wisdom required for governance, and 'ஊக்கம்' is the tireless enthusiasm to act. The word 'எஞ்சாமை' emphasizes that these four traits must never be lacking or diminished in a leader.

ai.literal: Promptness, learning, and possession of courage—these three should never depart from those who rule the land.
ai.translation: Promptness in action, learning, and decisiveness—these three qualities must never depart from those who rule the land.
ai.modern: சுறுசுறுப்பு, கல்வி, துணிவு ஆகிய இந்த மூன்றும் நாட்டை ஆளுபவர்களிடமிருந்து நீங்காமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three indispensable qualities of a successful ruler. 'தூங்காமை' literally means 'non-sleeping' or 'not delaying', representing promptness and the avoidance of sloth. 'கல்வி' denotes the acquisition of knowledge and wisdom, while 'துணிவுடைமை' is the possession of courage and decisiveness in taking action. The poet emphasizes that these three traits must never depart ('நீங்கா') from those who govern the earth ('நிலன் ஆள்பவர்க்கு', split metrically here as 'நிலனான் பவர்க்கு').

ai.literal: Virtue without-deviating, non-virtuous-things having-removed, valor unfailing, honor possessing-one, (is) the ruler.
ai.translation: A true ruler is one who never deviates from virtue, eliminates all that is evil, and possesses unfailing valor and honor.
ai.modern: அறநெறியிலிருந்து தவறாமல், தீமைகளை நீக்கி, வீரத்தில் குறையாத மானத்தைக் கொண்டிருப்பதே சிறந்த அரசாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of an ideal ruler or government. First, the ruler must steadfastly adhere to righteousness (அறன்) without slipping (இழுக்காது) and actively banish all forms of vice or injustice (அல்லவை நீக்கி). Second, the ruler must possess a sense of honor (மானம்) that never falters in courage or valor (மறன் இழுக்கா). By balancing moral integrity with strength and dignity, a ruler commands true authority.

ai.literal: And producing, and gathering, and guarding, and distributing the guarded (wealth), is what a capable government does.
ai.translation: An able government is one that can generate wealth, gather it, safeguard it, and distribute what has been safeguarded.
ai.modern: பொருளை உருவாக்கும் வழிகளை அறிதலும், அவ்வாறு வரும் பொருளைச் சேர்த்தலும், சேர்த்த பொருளைக் காத்தலும், காத்த பொருளைத் திட்டமிட்டுப் பகிர்ந்தளித்தலும் வல்லதே சிறந்த அரசு ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential economic duties of an effective state or ruler. First, 'iyaṟṟal' refers to creating or identifying new sources of revenue. Second, 'īṭṭal' is the actual collection and accumulation of these resources into the treasury. Third, 'kāttal' is safeguarding the collected wealth from external threats, waste, or corruption. Finally, 'vakuttal' is the wise allocation and distribution of the protected wealth for public welfare, defense, and development. A state that excels in all four of these functions is deemed capable and successful.

ai.literal: To sight easy, harsh-worded if he is not, highly praise will the king's land.
ai.translation: If a king is easy of access and not harsh in speech, the world will highly praise his land.
ai.modern: காண்பதற்கு எளியவனாகவும், கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பேசாதவனாகவும் ஒரு அரசன் இருந்தால், அவனது நாட்டை உலகத்தார் உயர்த்திப் பேசுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights two key qualities of an ideal ruler: accessibility and gentle communication. A leader must be easy for anyone to approach and meet without fear. Additionally, they must refrain from using harsh or offensive language when speaking to others. If a king rules with these qualities, the people of the world will highly praise and extol his land.

ai.literal: To those who are capable of protecting by giving with sweet words, this world is of the measure seen by their own word.
ai.translation: For a ruler who is able to give with sweet words and protect his subjects, this entire world will abide by his own command.
ai.modern: இனிய சொற்களைக் கூறி, கொடை கொடுத்துக் காக்கவல்ல அரசனுக்கு, இவ்வுலகம் அவனது சொல்லின்படி நடக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the qualities of a truly powerful and beloved ruler. A leader who speaks kindly, gives generously, and protects his people wins their complete devotion. For such a capable ruler, the entire world will willingly follow and obey his command. True authority and influence are shown to arise from benevolence and gentle speech rather than force.

ai.literal: Administering justice and protecting, the king, to the people, as god, will be regarded.
ai.translation: A ruler who administers justice and protects his subjects will be regarded as a god by his people.
ai.modern: நீதி தவறாமல் ஆட்சி செய்து மக்களைக் காப்பாற்றுகின்ற அரசன், மக்களுக்குக் கடவுள் என்று போற்றப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the highest ideal of leadership. A ruler's primary duties are twofold: administering impartial justice (முறைசெய்து) and safeguarding the welfare of the people (காப்பாற்றும்). When a leader performs these duties flawlessly, the people (மக்கட்கு) elevate him to the status of a divine protector (இறை). The word 'இறை' here signifies a god or a supreme guardian, showing that true divinity is perceived in the selfless act of protection and justice.

ai.literal: Under the protective umbrella of the king possessing the quality of bearing words that are bitter to the ear, the world will abide.
ai.translation: The world will rest under the protective umbrella of a ruler who has the noble quality of tolerating words that are bitter to his ears.
ai.modern: தன் காதுகளுக்குக் கசப்பாக இருக்கும் சொற்களையும் பொறுத்துக் கொள்ளும் குணம் கொண்ட அரசனுடைய குடையின் கீழ் இவ்வுலகம் தங்கி வாழும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of a ruler's tolerance toward criticism. The phrase 'cevi kaippa' means 'to make the ears bitter', referring to harsh but necessary truths or criticisms. A ruler who possesses the quality of patiently enduring such bitter words is highly revered. The 'kavikai' or protective umbrella represents the king's sovereign protection, and the poet states that the entire world will willingly seek shelter and abide under such a benevolent and tolerant ruler.

ai.literal: Generosity, compassion, an upright sceptre, and protecting subjects—he who possesses these four is a light to kings.
ai.translation: He who possesses these four qualities—generosity, compassion, a just rule, and care for his subjects—is a shining light among rulers.
ai.modern: கொடைத்தன்மை, கருணை, நேர்மையான ஆட்சி, குடிமக்களைக் காத்தல் ஆகிய நான்கையும் உடையவன் அரசர்களுக்குள் ஒளி போன்றவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential pillars of ideal governance. 'கொடை' represents the ruler's generosity, while 'அளி' denotes grace and compassion toward all living beings. 'செங்கோல்' (literally 'upright sceptre') signifies unbiased, righteous justice, and 'குடியோம்பல்' refers to the active protection and nurturing of the citizens. A ruler who embodies all four of these virtues stands out as a guiding light ('ஒளி') and an exemplar among other kings.
